question: At equal uniform-Budget20 selected-slab capacity, is terminal information better preserved by concentrating slabs inside the router's highest-weight route prefix than by spreading candidates over all native 16 routes?

intervention.definition: Only the first N routes from GGML's descending top-k router order are eligible for calibrated slabs or exact fallback. Retained native router weights are unchanged and omitted routes contribute zero; there is no renormalization in this screen.
intervention.scope: Research-only, width-one execution. Production defaults and the native router remain unchanged when the environment variable is absent.

measurements: selected slabs split by retained route where available
physical direct-read bytes and cold timings

gates.go: At least one route-limited arm restores the Budget24 first token, reduces KL by at least 50% versus route16 Budget20, and does not increase logical authoritative bytes.
gates.partial: An arm reduces KL by at least 50% and improves the Budget24-token margin but misses top-1; this may earn one separately preregistered retained-weight renormalization check, not a quality claim.
gates.no_go: No arm materially improves KL/margin or every arm remains wrong. Preserve the route-prefix result and do not claim the route axis is generally closed; only this unrenormalized global-prefix policy is closed.
gates.next_if_go: Run one full-generation tool arm using the winning route count plus the validated schema rescue; require a valid tool call and lower bytes before held-out quality validation.
gates.production: No production transplant from this discovery fixture.

limitations: This screen uses a behaviorally successful Budget24 reference rather than native exact terminal logits.
One global route count cannot establish layer-adaptive route allocation.
Omitted-route weights are not renormalized; conclusions do not automatically transfer to a renormalized router.
Cold token-sequential timing is not serving throughput.
